evidence: The agent agreed latestArtifact trusts forgeable body content but deferred the whole thing to zai-review-trust-6yp, arguing a latestArtifact-only fix would be 'worse than none'. One round later (F12) the agent itself shipped the narrow fix (fork call site passes latestArtifact: null), which needed no identity mechanism and closed the silencing path, so the deferral argument did not hold.
guidance_note: When deferring a security finding to a general ticket, first ask whether this PR's new code can stop consuming the untrusted value on its own path; a narrow 'don't read it here' fix needs no general solution.

evidence: In the round-0 hunk, renderNotReviewedBody was evaluated as the body: argument inside the try, so its unknown-reason throw landed in the host-failure catch and became a warning on an exit-0 run. c52dbdd hoisted it to a const above the try and added a test that drives the bad reason through announceNotReviewed.
guidance_note: When a function documents a throw as a loud programming-error guard, check that no caller evaluates it inside a catch-all try.

evidence: The original comment said 'listReviews pages ascend, so the last assignment wins' in a function shared with Gitea, making page order load-bearing on an unverified guarantee. c52dbdd keys on the highest review id, which is one of the reviewer's suggestions, and a test serves a descending page.
guidance_note: When adding a 'latest' derivation to a loop whose other outputs are order-independent sums, key it on an explicit ordering field instead of arrival order.

evidence: The README recommended pull_request_target with no caveat beside a Quickstart that checks out head.sha, which is the pwn-request pattern. c52dbdd dropped pull_request_target from the README, CLAUDE.md, and the runtime warning, and added an explicit warning paragraph.
guidance_note: Before recommending a workflow trigger in docs, check it against the repo's own Quickstart checkout step for the pull_request_target + head.sha combination.

evidence: The round-0 hunk moved summarizePriorReviews, which calls core.setFailed on error, ahead of prIsFromFork, so a transient listReviews error could fail a fork skip that previously could not fail. c52dbdd restored the fork gate to run first. Its best-effort helper was later deleted in 8a99d77 when the fork path stopped reading the key.
guidance_note: When reordering a fetch ahead of an 'unconditional' gate, list the gate's prior failure modes and confirm the new dependency adds none.

evidence: This duplicates F5 on the same line, and the same c52dbdd change fixes it: the fork gate decides from pr alone and runs first.
parseAgentArtifact hard-coded the marker literal in its regex while renderNotReviewedBody used NOT_REVIEWED_MARKER_PREFIX. c52dbdd builds NOT_REVIEWED_MARKER_RE from the escaped prefix.
guidance_note: When writing a reader for a marker the same module writes, build the reader's pattern from the writer's constant at the start.

evidence: run.js retyped 'fork' and 'round-cap' instead of referencing NOT_REVIEWED_REASONS. The reviewer's NOT_REVIEWED_REASONS[0] carries no meaning and depends on array order, so the agent's named frozen object ({FORK, ROUND_CAP}) is the better cure for the same diagnosis.
guidance_note: When exporting a closed enumeration, make it a named object and import it at every call site in the same commit.

evidence: The read-then-post race is real. Documenting the concurrency group as a precondition was one of the reviewer's two options, and the agent's reason for not doing compare-and-swap holds: GitHub has no atomic primitive, and the race can only produce a duplicate, never silence.
guidance_note: When adding an idempotency check over a read-then-write API, state the concurrency precondition in the same commit.

evidence: The fork notice message names no remedy, so 'names the cause and its remedy' overclaimed. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent accepted and reworded in c52dbdd.

Flag false positive: the claim that a fork notice cannot post on pull_request and needs workflow_run was already in 5aeb47f's README ('One case cannot be delivered...'). c52dbdd's F4 fix only removed pull_request_target. The premise fails because pull_request runs from forks receive no repository secrets, so GITHUB_REVIEW_TOKEN is empty there. The agent pushed back with that reason and documented the non-escape-hatch.

This is F1's forgeable-marker gap again, narrowed to the fork path. F1 was deferred, and c52dbdd (F5's fix) kept the fork path reading the untrusted key through latestArtifactBestEffort. Instead of the reviewer's reason==='fork' branch, the agent passed latestArtifact: null at the fork call site, which also deleted the helper.
guidance_note: When a deferred security gap meets a fix that rewires the same value, re-check in that fix whether the new path still consumes the untrusted value.

evidence: Flag false positive: the reason-only comparison (latestArtifact.reason === notice.reason) existed since 5aeb47f, and 8a99d77 only added a comment above it. The stale-message scenario is real because the round-cap message varies with the de-rated cap. 84a6477 keys the check on the rendered body.
guidance_note: When designing a dedup key, key on the full rendered content rather than a category label, unless the content is invariant for that category.

evidence: 8a99d77 (F12's fix) introduced 'a same-repo PR's reviews come only from accounts with push access' in CLAUDE.md, README, and run.js as the rationale for keeping the round-cap key. On a public repo, posting a COMMENT review needs only read access. The agent corrected all three to state the exposure, which is one of the reviewer's two options.
guidance_note: When a fix's rationale rests on a platform permission claim, verify the claim before writing it into three docs.

evidence: 8a99d77's security fix lived in a hand-assembled latestArtifact: null argument at one run.js call site, and no test covered that call site. Instead of the requested integration test, the agent added forkNotice/roundCapNotice constructors so the pairing cannot be written wrong.
guidance_note: When a security fix is a single argument value at a call site, encode it in a named constructor or test that call site in the same commit.

evidence: Flag false positive: the catch-block warning has given only fork-specific advice for both callers since 5aeb47f ('use pull_request_target or workflow_run'). c52dbdd changed the trigger named but not its fork-only scope, and 8a99d77 did not touch it. The agent moved the hint onto the notice value as postFailureHint instead of adding a reason branch.
guidance_note: When a shared catch block serves several callers, check its remedy text against each caller's possible causes.

evidence: Flag false positive: dist/ was rebuilt in every commit, and the reviewer could not see it because the repo's EXCLUDE_PATTERNS drops dist/**. Nothing about 78dc3fb caused this finding. The agent showed git log and stat output for dist/ and a clean npm run build diff, then filed the silent exclusion as zai-review-prompt-2tx.

84a6477 (F16's fix) made the round-cap hint avoid naming a cause it cannot know, but wrote a forkNotice postFailureHint asserting the no-secrets cause outright. prIsFromFork does not depend on the trigger, so the fork path is reachable under workflow_run. The agent admitted 'committing the exact defect I had just fixed one function below', and 6277d4d fixed it.
guidance_note: When fixing a diagnostic so it names only knowable causes, apply the same check to every sibling diagnostic written in that commit.

evidence: Flag false positive: 'before any credential is read' became false in the original 5aeb47f, when the fork path started posting through reviewOctokit, and 78dc3fb was a comment-trim commit. The agent qualified it to 'AI credential' in the README and CLAUDE.md.
guidance_note: When a feature adds a new action to an existing path, grep the docs for invariants describing that path and re-check each one.

evidence: CLAUDE.md's '{reason, message}' notice shape went stale when 84a6477 (the F15/F16 constructors) added latestArtifact and postFailureHint to the value. The later paragraph listed four fields, so the doc contradicted itself.
guidance_note: When a fix adds fields to a value whose shape is spelled out in docs, grep for the old shape literal and update every instance.

evidence: 84a6477 (F13's fix) added body to parseAgentArtifact's not-reviewed arm for the body-keyed dedup, but CLAUDE.md's documented return type still read {kind:'not-reviewed', reason}.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a function's return shape, update the documented type signature in the same commit.

evidence: After 8a99d77 (F12's fix), the fork notice reposts on every push. That commit added a later paragraph saying so, but left the earlier unqualified 'It posts once per cause rather than once per push' in place.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a documented universal property hold for only some cases, qualify the original sentence instead of appending a correction below it.

evidence: 6277d4d (F18's fix) split the hint into exactly pull_request vs workflow_run and its comment claimed 'both branches are named'. resolveReviewTarget documents workflow_dispatch as a third trigger that reaches this path. 2ea62d0 made the second branch the complement of the first.
guidance_note: When splitting a message by case, make the last branch the complement ('any other trigger') instead of enumerating the cases you happen to know.

evidence: Flag false positive: the warn-only catch for both callers dates from 5aeb47f, and 6277d4d only changed the fork hint text. The premise holds because the fork justification (no permission can ever fix it) does not apply to the round cap, which only same-repo PRs reach. The agent also noted submitReview already throws on the same refusal, then added reportPostFailure to the notice value.
guidance_note: When a failure policy is justified by one caller's constraint, check whether that constraint holds for every caller sharing the policy.

narrative: The PR adds a NOT REVIEWED notice for fork and round-cap skips, and it ran into the 5-round cap; round 5 is the round-cap notice itself. Most of round 0's findings were original-design gaps and were fixed well. Every later round mixed pre-existing gaps (F13, F16, F19, F24) with defects the agent's own fixes introduced: false trust-boundary rationale (F14), stale doc shapes (F20, F21, F22), and a hint fix applied to only one sibling (F18 then F23). No round was purely fix-caused, so avoidable_rounds is 0. Still, 8 of the 14 post-round-0 findings trace to earlier fixes or to the F1 deferral.
guidance_observations: Each fix rewrote prose in CLAUDE.md, README, and code comments together, and most fix-caused findings were doc text the fix left stale or got wrong. A grep for the changed concept across all three after each fix would have caught them.
The F1 deferral cost a round: one round later, the narrow 'don't consume the untrusted key on this path' fix proved cheap and self-contained.

The agent repeatedly fixed a defect in one diagnostic and repeated it in its sibling written in the same commit (F16 then F18, F18 then F23), which points to a missing 'sweep the siblings' step before pushing a fix.
